To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

inorganic arsenic induces axial skeletal malformations in hamsters and that these malformations are associated with delayed elevation and closure of the neural folds and a paucity or absence of cephalic paraxial mesenchyme.
the teratogenic response in hamsters is associated with a delay in elevation and closure of the neural folds and with a deficiency in cephalic mesenchyme.
arsenic-induced axial skeletal (i.e. dysraphic) disorders in the golden hamster are associated with a delay in neural-tube closure and a deficiency of cephalic paraxial mesenchyme.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the teratogenic potential of arsenic, a ubiquitous environmental contaminant.
the mechanisms by which arsenic induces axial skeletal defects in the developing golden hamster embryo.
the teratogenic effects of arsenic and the mechanisms of action of arsenic in the production of axial skeletal malformations in the golden hamster.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the teratogenic response to inorganic arsenic is related to the inorganic form and not the methylated form of arsenic.
arsenic is teratogenic in hamsters and the mechanism of action may be related to interference with the development of the axial skeleton.
arsenic-induced dysraphic disorders in the golden hamster are due to a direct toxic effect of the arsenic compound on the paraxial cephalic mesenchyme.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the teratogenic response to sodium arsenate in the hamster embryo is associated with a delay in the formation of cephalic paraxial mesenchyme.
arsenic is an embryotoxin and that the mechanism of arsenic-induced embryonic toxicity is related to the inhibition of protein synthesis.
arsenic-induced teratogenicity in the hamster is related to the inhibition of the paraxial-mesoderm differentiation and to the subsequent failure of the neural tube to close.
The main takeaway from our work is that
arsenic can cause skeletal malformations in the embryo.
arsenic can cause a range of birth defects, including spina bifida and other neural tube defects, as well as craniofacial defects.
arsenic exposure during the first 2 weeks of pregnancy in hamsters results in the production of cranio-schisis with encephalocoelic and cranioschistic defects in a large percentage of offspring.
